text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL TREASURY POSTS RECORD DEFICIT IN 1996
Brazil's National Treasury had a record deficit of 9.0 billion reais in 1996 as a result of higher interest rate expenses and personnel costs.
-- C. CORREA, BRADESCO BRING CHANGE TO ALPARGATAS
Brazilian construction firm Camargo Correa and bank Bradesco announced they reached a 10-year accord with shareholders to take control of and restructure Sao Paulo Alpargatas.
-- BRAZIL'S EMBRATUR LOSES ITS STARS
State tourism company Embratur has decided to rethink its star system of classifying Brazil's hotels and plans to re-evaluate inns, a move that has unleashed a battle with hotel owners.
O GLOBO
-- PMDB PARTY REACHES ACCORD TO VOTE ON RE-ELECTION TODAY

The Brazilian government and PMDB party leaders reached an accord to vote today in a special congressional committee on a constitutional amendment that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election in 1998.
-- SHOOT-OUT WITH LANDLESS LEAVES 12 DEAD IN NORTH
A gun fight between landless farmers and armed guards in the northern state of Para left at least 12 people dead, according to preliminary information received by the Justice Ministry.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOVERNMENT SAYS HAS 298 VOTES IN FAVOR OF RE-ELECTION

Brazilian government officials said they have garnered 298 of the 308 votes needed to pass a re-election amendment in Congress' Chamber of Deputies but a survey by the newspaper reveals only 215 deputies back the bill.
-- LANDLESS CONFLICT LEAVES AT SEVEN DEAD IN PARA STATE
A clash between security guards and landless peasants squatting on a ranch has left at least seven people dead, while unconfirmed reports said the number may reach as high as 15 killed.
-- CARDOSO SAYS "STREET" SUPPORTS RE-ELECTION
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said he is not afraid of congressional opposition to re-election, saying "the street" supports the idea.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
